examples.title: Amplitude Modulation - Message x Carrier
examples.description: A slow message sine (0.2 Hz) multiplies a fast carrier sine (2 Hz) to form a double-sideband product. The scope overlays message, their product and the carrier so the carrier riding inside the message envelope is visible.

examples.title: Bus Assignment Demo
examples.description: Groups a position vector and a scalar count into a bus (busCreator), replaces the 'count' member with a new value (busAssignment), then reads both members back out (busSelector). 'pos' passes through unchanged; 'count' is overwritten.

examples.title: Chirp Frequency Response - Low-pass
examples.description: A linear chirp sweeps 0.1 -> 3 Hz over 20 s into a first-order low-pass 1/(0.15 s + 1). The scope overlays the raw chirp and the filtered output: as the sweep frequency climbs, the low-pass rolls the amplitude off, so the filtered trace shrinks while the input stays at full amplitude.

examples.title: Coulomb & Viscous Friction Demo
examples.description: A sinusoidal velocity drives a Coulomb & Viscous Friction block (y = Gain*u + Offset*sign(u)). Scopes compare the input velocity and the resulting friction force, showing the viscous slope plus the Coulomb jump at zero.

examples.title: Logic Gates Demo
examples.description: Logic Gates Demo - AND, OR, XOR, NOT with constant inputs and scope outputs

examples.title: Nonlinear Elements - Saturation vs Dead-zone
examples.description: A sine of amplitude 1.5 is fed through two static nonlinearities. Saturation clips it to +/-1 (flat tops), while the dead-zone [-0.5,0.5] holds the output at zero near the origin and passes the offset excess beyond. The scope overlays the input with both shaped signals.

examples.title: PID Demo - P vs PI vs PID
Second-Order Responses - Damping Comparison
examples.description: Second-order step responses: the same unit step drives three plants that differ only in their damping. Underdamped 1/(s^2+0.4s+1) rings, overdamped 1/(s^2+3s+2) crawls, resonant 4/(s^2+0.5s+4) overshoots strongly. The scope overlays the three so the damping regimes can be compared at a glance.

examples.title: Signal Utilities Demo
examples.description: Demonstrates four signal-routing niche blocks: width (element count of a vector), signalConversion (identity pass-through), enumeratedConstant (a fixed enumeration value) and assignment (write elements of a base vector at given indices).

examples.title: Acausal Brake
examples.description:
Acausal rotational demo: a signal-actuated brake stops a spinning flywheel.

Physics: the flywheel (Inertia J = 1 kg.m2) starts at w0 = 10 rad/s. The RotBrake applies a friction torque to ground whose peak magnitude is set by its signal input (constant 4 N.m). The friction is tanh-regularised around w = 0 (parameter w_eps), so the model is event-free and integrates smoothly with a fixed-step solver: J dw/dt = -tau_brake(w). The flywheel therefore decelerates and settles at rest (w -> 0 in about 2.5 s). The RotSpeedSensor measures the shaft speed; the Scope plots w(t) and the ToWorkspace block exports it as the variable 'w'.

Wiring: the three rotational flanges (RotBrake, Inertia, RotSpeedSensor) share ONE physical node -- the green pins joined by the vertical wire on the left. This is an undirected acausal connection (no arrows): torques sum to zero and the speed is common. The constant signal comes in from the top into the brake's actuation input; the sensor's signal output leaves at the bottom to the scope and the workspace export -- so signal wires and the physical bus stay on opposite sides.

examples.title: Acausal Contact (ElastoGap)
examples.description: Acausal 1-D contact demo: a mass driven by a constant force meets a compliant one-sided contact (ElastoGap) with an initial gap. While the gap is open the mass moves freely; once closed, the contact acts as a spring-damper that pushes back -- a unilateral (non-penetrating) contact, regularised so it stays event-free. The three translational flanges share one physical node. The Scope plots the mass position; ToWorkspace exports it.

examples.title: Acausal DC Motor
examples.description:
Acausal DC-motor demo (mixed electrical + mechanical): a 1 V source drives an armature (Resistor R = 1, Inductor L = 1) feeding an EMF converter (back-emf v = k w, torque tau = k i, k = 1); the EMF spins a flywheel (Inertia J = 1) loaded by a rotational damper (d = 1) held to a rotational reference. The motor accelerates until the electromagnetic torque balances the viscous load, reaching a steady shaft speed. NOTE: mixing an electrical DAE island with a mechanical island requires the DAE solver. The Scope plots shaft speed; ToWorkspace exports it as w.

Layout: an electrical loop on the left (Resistor + Inductor + EMF across the top, constant source below, ground at bottom) and a mechanical column to its right (flywheel, speed sensor, damper) whose flanges share the EMF shaft; the sensor signal drops to the scope and workspace stacked to the right.

examples.title: Acausal EMF DC Motor
examples.description:
Acausal DC-motor demo (mixed electrical + mechanical): a constant voltage drives a resistor and an EMF converter (v = k*w, tau = k*i); the EMF spins a flywheel (Inertia) loaded by a rotational damper and held to a rotational reference. The motor accelerates until the electrical torque balances the viscous load, reaching a steady speed. NOTE: mixing an electrical DAE island with a mechanical island requires the DAE solver. The Scope plots shaft speed; ToWorkspace exports it.

Layout: a roomy electrical loop on the left (Resistor + EMF on top, source below, ground at bottom) and a tight mechanical column to its right (flywheel, speed sensor, damper) whose left flanges share one physical node. The flywheel sits above the EMF so its top flange joins the column with a single clean elbow; the reference sits off the damper, and the sensor signal drops to the scope and workspace stacked to the right at the sensor's output level.

examples.title: Acausal Freewheel
examples.description: Acausal one-way-clutch demo: a prescribed rotating source drives a flywheel through a Freewheel (overrunning clutch). Torque is transmitted only while the source overruns the flywheel; when the source slows, the clutch releases and the flywheel coasts on its own inertia. The Scope plots flywheel speed; ToWorkspace exports it.

examples.title: Acausal Half-Wave Rectifier
examples.description: Acausal half-wave rectifier: a sine AC source (via a SignalVoltage) feeds a diode into an RC load. The diode conducts only on positive half-cycles and the capacitor smooths the output, so the load voltage is a rectified, ripple-smoothed waveform. The Scope plots the output voltage; ToWorkspace exports it.

examples.title: Acausal Mass-Spring-Damper
examples.description: Acausal mass-spring-damper: a mass connected to a wall through a parallel spring and damper, released from an initial offset, oscillates and decays to its equilibrium position -- a classic second-order response. The translational flanges share physical nodes. The Scope plots the mass position; ToWorkspace exports it.

examples.title: Acausal RC low-pass in a subsystem
examples.description: A self-contained acausal RC low-pass circuit grouped inside a plain subsystem (Tier 1: acausal components inside a subsystem). The subsystem 'RC_Lowpass' holds a sinusoidal voltage source, a resistor, a capacitor to ground and a voltage sensor wired with physical wires; it exposes the sensed capacitor voltage as its single output. On simulation NFlow.internal.acausalExpand recurses into the subsystem and lowers the physical wires into a nested physicalIsland (the engine simulates it exactly like a top-level island). The Scope plots the filtered capacitor voltage and ToWorkspace exports it. tau = R*C = 100*1e-3 = 0.1 s.

examples.title: Acausal RLC Circuit
examples.description: Acausal series RLC circuit: a constant voltage source drives a resistor, inductor and capacitor in series to ground. The inductor and capacitor exchange energy while the resistor damps it, so the capacitor voltage rings and settles to the source value -- a damped second-order electrical response. The Scope plots the capacitor voltage; ToWorkspace exports it.

examples.title: Acausal Rotational Drivetrain
examples.description: Acausal rotational drivetrain: two inertias coupled by an ideal gear, driven by a constant torque and loaded by a rotational damper to a fixed reference. The gear scales speed and torque by its ratio; the output shaft accelerates to the steady speed where drive torque balances damping. The Scope plots the output-shaft speed; ToWorkspace exports it.

examples.title: Acausal Series RLC (AC)
examples.description: Acausal series RLC circuit driven by a sinusoidal voltage source. The source feeds a resistor, an inductor, a current sensor and a capacitor in series to ground. After the initial transient the capacitor voltage settles into a steady sinusoid, phase-shifted and scaled by the frequency response of the second-order circuit; the current sensor reports the loop current i = C dVc/dt. The Scope plots the capacitor voltage and the loop current; ToWorkspace exports both.

examples.title: Acausal Thermal Heatsink
examples.description: Acausal thermal RC demo: a heated thermal mass (HeatCapacitor) loses heat through a thermal resistance to a fixed ambient temperature. The body temperature relaxes exponentially toward ambient -- a first-order thermal (RC) response. The heat-port nodes are the physical connections. The Scope plots the body temperature; ToWorkspace exports it.

examples.title: Planar Double Pendulum
examples.description: Planar 2-D multibody demo: a double pendulum -- two rigid bodies joined by revolute joints, hanging from a fixed world frame -- swings under gravity. Its motion is chaotic and highly sensitive to initial conditions. Constraints are Baumgarte-stabilised. (Planar island: simulation only, no code generation.) The Scope plots a tip coordinate; ToWorkspace exports it.

examples.title: Planar Pendulum
examples.description: Planar 2-D single rod pendulum: a uniform rod (length 1, mass 1) pivoted at one end to a fixed world frame, released horizontally, swings under gravity. The body angle follows the physical-pendulum equation I_pivot phi'' = -m g d cos(phi). The Scope plots the angle; ToWorkspace exports it.

examples.title: Planar Reaction Wheel
examples.description:
Planar 2-D multibody demo: a reaction wheel. Two free bodies -- a platform (I = 0.5) and a wheel (I = 2) -- are coupled only by an internal actuator torque (tau = 1). With no external anchor and no gravity, total angular momentum is conserved: the actuator spins the wheel one way while the platform recoils the other, their angular accelerations in inverse ratio to their inertias (alpha = tau / I). (Planar island: simulation only, no code generation.) ToWorkspace exports both angular speeds as W0 (platform) and W1 (wheel).

Layout: the gravity-free world sits at the left; the two bodies stack in the middle joined by the relative-torque actuator; each body has a velocity sensor (axis omega) whose signal drops to its ToWorkspace sink on the right.

examples.title: Planar Rigid Triple Pendulum
examples.description: Runnable planar multibody demo stored as a native mechanical island: three uniform rigid rods are connected in series by frictionless revolute joints and released horizontally under gravity. Keeping the already-lowered island in the example avoids an interpreter-thread dependency when Run is pressed. The real-time XY Scope animates the end-point trajectory while the Scope overlays all three absolute rod angles.

examples.title: Planar Spring Pendulum

It swings and bounces as a spring pendulum and settles at the static spring stretch. Constraints are Baumgarte-stabilised. (Planar island: simulation only.) The Scope plots the body's vertical position; ToWorkspace exports it.

examples.title: Medical Ventilator - Bi-level (PC-AC) with simulated patient
examples.description: Bi-level (PC-AC) mechanical ventilation on a single-compartment lung. Airway pressure alternates between Pinsp and PEEP; the lung (resistance R, compliance C) responds as a first-order system, giving the decelerating inspiratory flow and the tidal volume of pressure-controlled ventilation. A periodic patient effort (Pmus) is added at each inspiration onset to emulate an assisted breath. Scopes show Pressure / Flow / Volume like a ventilator screen; the XY scope draws the dynamic pressure-volume loop. Settings: PEEP 5, Pinsp 18 cmH2O, RR 15/min, Ti 1.2 s (Width 30%), R 10 cmH2O.s/L, C 0.05 L/cmH2O (tau = R*C = 0.5 s) -> Vt ~ 0.6 L.
